reason: ANTI-STRAWMAN, done correctly this time. MAPS trains on every marker the 6 TRAINING cohorts share - not intersected with the held-out cohort, which is what made check 2 degenerate - and at test time the held-out cohort's missing markers are zero-filled. This is what a careful practitioner actually does: use as much of the panel as training allows and accept imputation at test. It is strictly more training signal than core-9
note: the gap between this arm and core-9 measures what MAPS gains from a wider training panel it cannot fully use at test time. On the Sorin fold the training intersection is much larger than 9 because Sorin's 17-marker panel is no longer in it - that fold is the interesting one

reason: the naive thing a practitioner actually does. Design idea 2 says a zero means 'negative', which is a different and false claim than 'not measured'.
